Assessment: The July 27, 2022 FOMC statement is hawkish (75 bp hike to 2.25–2.50%, guidance for “ongoing increases,” and balance-sheet runoff ramping to $60B Treasuries/$35B MBS in September). However, Beige Book reports point to softening demand via the credit channel: multiple Districts note weakening residential loan demand alongside increased usage of revolving credit lines. This mix implies tighter bank intermediation and a cooling housing sector, which should restrain growth and inflation at the margin. Net: still hawkish, but tempered by Beige Book evidence of slowing credit-sensitive activity.
